clue.text: For whom Henry should have commissioned Stubbs, not Holbein ?

definitions.text: For whom Henry should have commissioned Stubbs, not Holbein ?

parts.words: For whom Henry should have commissioned Stubbs, not Holbein ?
parts.note: Henry VIII's unkind nickname for his fourth wife likened her to a horse, so a horse painter like Stubbs would have suited her better than the portraitist Holbein

explanation.surface: A question about which court painter Henry VIII ought to have hired for a portrait.
explanation.walkthrough: Holbein painted Anne of Cleves for Henry VIII; disappointed in the flesh, Henry is said to have called her a mare from Flanders. George Stubbs was the great English painter of horses.
explanation.definitionFit: The nickname Henry VIII gave Anne of Cleves, his fourth queen, whom he found unattractive.

clue.text: Quarrel re nuclear risk

explanation.surface: A dispute about the dangers of nuclear power.
explanation.definitionFit: To fall out is to have a row; radioactive dust settling after a nuclear explosion carries the same name.

clue.text: Range and directions

parts.note: E and S are the compass points east and south

explanation.surface: A mountain range and the way to get there.
explanation.definitionFit: The South American mountain chain is a range of peaks.

clue.text: Company may get the wind up, but this gives a sense of security

definitions.text: Company may get the wind up, but this gives a sense of security

parts.words: Company may get the wind up, but this gives a sense of security
parts.note: reads as a nervous firm being reassured, but means a loan document that keeps a lender secured if the company is wound up

explanation.surface: A frightened company finds comfort in feeling secure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get the wind up' looks like panic, but it hints at a company being wound up; the holder of this bond is a secured creditor, and the bond itself is a 'security'.
explanation.definitionFit: A bond issued by a company, secured on its assets, so the lender is protected in a liquidation.

clue.text: Seldom done, never well done

explanation.surface: A remark about something that hardly ever happens, perhaps a steak.
explanation.definitionFit: Something seldom happening is uncommon; meat that is never well cooked is underdone, as a steak can be.

clue.text: Graduates to fellow — makes old-style Jumbo

parts.note: MAs are Masters of Arts, university graduates
a don is a fellow of a college at Oxford or Cambridge

explanation.surface: Graduates going on to become fellows somehow resemble a big old elephant.
explanation.walkthrough: Jumbo was a famous elephant; 'old-style' points to the extinct elephant-like beast.
explanation.definitionFit: An extinct prehistoric relative of the elephant, so an elephant of an older kind.

clue.text: Send stop-watch back

indicators.note: back tells us to read the stop-watch word from its end to its start

parts.note: a stop-watch is a timer

explanation.surface: An instruction to return a stop-watch.
explanation.definitionFit: To remit money is to send it, as a payment by post.

clue.text: Bird in a circle of fire

parts.note: something on fire is flaming
the letter O is round like a circle

explanation.surface: A bird trapped in a ring of flames, as in a circus act.
explanation.definitionFit: A pink wading bird with long legs, found in lakes and lagoons.

clue.text: French city gave birth to its weight in gold

definitions.text: French city gave birth to its weight in gold

parts.words: French city gave birth to its weight in gold
parts.note: the system of weights used for gold and silver takes its name from this town in Champagne, so the town gave birth to it

explanation.surface: A French city produced its own weight in gold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Its weight in gold' sounds like great value, but it is the weight system for precious metals, troy weight, named after the city.
explanation.definitionFit: A city in Champagne, northern France, whose fairs gave troy weight its name.

clue.text: Beetles spotted as high-class egg-layers

explanation.surface: Spotted beetles described as posh hens.
explanation.definitionFit: Small red spotted beetles; read as two words, ladies' birds would be upper-class layers of eggs.

clue.text: Dusty, half-hearted, but still in the running

indicators.note: one of the two central letters is lost, so the heart of the word is cut by half

parts.note: a miller is covered in flour, and Dusty Miller is a nickname for anyone called Miller

explanation.surface: A dusty, listless runner who is nevertheless still competing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-hearted' drops one of the two Ls at the centre of MILLER.
explanation.definitionFit: A runner who races over a mile is a competitor in a race.

clue.text: Might Cesario alternatively do wrong to love him ?

definitions.text: Might Cesario alternatively do wrong to love him ?

parts.note: or introduces an alternative
to sin is to do wrong
love is nil in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A question whether Cesario might be wrong to love a certain man.
explanation.walkthrough: In Twelfth Night, Viola disguises herself as the page Cesario and falls in love with the Duke she serves, a love that looks wrong for a young man.
explanation.definitionFit: The Duke of Illyria in Shakespeare's Twelfth Night, loved by Viola while she is disguised as Cesario.

clue.text: Hull (as against Halifax?) mortgage

parts.note: two Yorkshire towns: Halifax was a building society lending on houses, while a ship's hull can be pledged as security for a loan

explanation.surface: A comparison of mortgages from two Yorkshire towns, Hull and Halifax.
explanation.walkthrough: Hull and Halifax look like places; the Halifax was a big British building society giving home loans, while 'hull' is the ship's keel and bottom pledged in this old maritime loan.
explanation.definitionFit: A loan to a shipowner secured on the ship itself, repayable only if the voyage succeeds.

clue.text: One for Mr. Micawber's book in Australia ?

definitions.text: One for Mr. Micawber's book in Australia ?

parts.words: One for Mr. Micawber's book in Australia ?
parts.note: Dickens's Micawber kept waiting for something to appear unexpectedly, finally found luck in Australia, and a surprise is 'one for the book'

explanation.surface: A question about what Mr Micawber would record in his book in Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: Mr Micawber in David Copperfield always trusted that something would turn up, and he prospers after emigrating to Australia; a surprise is called a 'turn-up for the book'.
explanation.definitionFit: An unexpected stroke of luck, the surprise Micawber was forever expecting.

clue.text: Remembrance of a girl or two

explanation.surface: Remembering a girl, or perhaps two of them.
explanation.walkthrough: Ophelia in Hamlet says the herb is 'for remembrance'.
explanation.definitionFit: The herb is the emblem of memory in Hamlet; it is also one girl's name, or the names Rose and Mary together.

clue.text: Modern style of hart seeking cooling streams

definitions.text: Modern style of hart seeking cooling streams

parts.words: Modern style of hart seeking cooling streams
parts.note: the Psalm's deer panting for water brooks is overheated and gasping, while the same two words name skimpy shorts

explanation.surface: A fashionable way for a deer to go looking for cool water.
explanation.walkthrough: Psalm 42 says 'As the hart panteth after the water brooks'; a hart that is hot and pants gives the 1970s fashion of very short shorts.
explanation.definitionFit: Very short, tight shorts for women, a fashion of the 1970s.

clue.text: Peter has to go through the motions at the Christmas treat

parts.note: Peter Pan, J M Barrie's boy who never grew up
to mime is to act out movements without words

explanation.surface: Peter must act a part at the Christmas party.
explanation.walkthrough: A pantomime is a British family stage show put on at Christmas, with comic songs and cross-dressing; 'has' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A British comic family play staged in the festive season, a seasonal outing for children.

clue.text: What's a circle? Answer verbally or by demonstration

definitions.text: What's a circle? Answer verbally or by demonstration

parts.words: What's a circle? Answer verbally or by demonstration
parts.note: you can explain a circle in words, or draw one with compasses: both senses of the same verb

explanation.surface: An exam question asking for a circle to be explained in words or shown.
explanation.walkthrough: In geometry one 'describes' a circle by drawing it, so the verb covers both telling and tracing.
explanation.definitionFit: To give an account in words, or in geometry to trace out a figure.

clue.text: Plagued, the good man's in deeper trouble

indicators.note: the saint is placed inside the rearranged letters
deeper in trouble, so its letters are disturbed into a new order

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for saint, a good man

explanation.surface: Someone plagued, a good man sinking deeper into trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deeper trouble' reads as a phrase, but 'trouble' is the anagram signal on 'deeper' and 'in' sets the saint inside the result.
explanation.definitionFit: Plagued and harassed both mean annoyed persistently.

clue.text: Temple tree shaken by nabobs

explanation.surface: A temple tree being shaken by rich men.
explanation.walkthrough: Nabobs were Britons who made fortunes in India; 'to shake the pagoda tree' meant to get rich quickly there, pagodas also being gold coins.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiered Eastern tower used as a temple; the 'tree' is the one in the phrase for growing rich in India.

clue.text: One can go rambling in this material

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the run of words across their joins

explanation.surface: A fabric loose enough to go walking in.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft fabric or yarn made from the hair of a goat or rabbit.

clue.text: Win highest honour outside the hive perhaps

indicators.note: the honour goes round the other piece, enclosing it

parts.note: the ace is the top honour card in a suit

indicators.note: perhaps tells us the hive's letters could take another form

explanation.surface: Winning the top award outside the beehive.
explanation.walkthrough: In card games the honours are the top cards, and the ace ranks highest; 'perhaps' shuffles the hive and 'outside' wraps the ace round it.
explanation.definitionFit: To win something is to attain it through effort.

clue.text: In the main a fighter

parts.note: a main is an old name for a cockfighting match, not the sea where a warship would fight

explanation.surface: A warship fighting on the open sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The main' suggests the ocean and a naval fighter; in cockfighting a 'main' is a series of bouts between birds.
explanation.definitionFit: A cock bred and trained for fighting, which is matched against others in a main.

clue.text: Is this sweep out of work ?

definitions.text: Is this sweep out of work ?

parts.words: Is this sweep out of work ?
parts.note: a chimney sweep who is not working would not be sooty, and the word also completes 'sweep' as a total victory

explanation.surface: A question whether a chimney sweep has no job.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'clean sweep' is a complete win; a sweep off work is free of soot.
explanation.definitionFit: Free of dirt, as a sweep away from the soot would be, and the word that makes a 'sweep' total.

clue.text: Chemical evidence of reefer-smoking ?

parts.note: a smoked joint of cannabis leaves cinders, so the drug's slang name plus the residue name a compound

explanation.surface: Chemical traces proving someone smoked a cannabis cigarette.
explanation.walkthrough: A reefer is a cannabis cigarette; pot is cannabis and ash is what smoking leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: Potassium carbonate or other potassium compounds, used in fertiliser and soap.

clue.text: The tiny mites get the vehicle in top condition

indicators.note: the vehicle goes inside the top condition

parts.note: A1 means first-class, written AI in letters
a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: Tiny mites in a car that is in excellent condition.
explanation.definitionFit: The scientific name for mites and ticks.

clue.text: A piece that is played

explanation.surface: A bit of something that someone plays.
explanation.definitionFit: A portion or section of a whole; also an actor's role in a play.

clue.text: "With mirth in funeral and with in marriage" (Hamlet)

definitions.text: "With mirth in funeral and with in marriage" (Hamlet)

parts.words: "With mirth in funeral and with in marriage" (Hamlet)
parts.note: the missing word in Claudius's line balances mirth at a burial with mourning song at a wedding

explanation.surface: A line from Hamlet with one word left out.
explanation.walkthrough: Claudius, marrying his dead brother's widow, says 'With mirth in funeral and with dirge in marriage'; the gap is filled by the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A mournful song or lament for the dead, the opposite of the mirth in the line.

clue.text: Lacking spirit for conversion, i.e. a tinman

indicators.note: the letters are offered to be converted into a new form

explanation.surface: A tin man, lacking a soul, needs converting.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tin Man of Oz wanted a heart; here 'for conversion' rearranges I E A TINMAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Lifeless, without a soul or living spirit.

clue.text: An arty type is within-put him out

indicators.note: the word is goes inside the arty type

parts.note: an aesthete is someone devoted to art and beauty

explanation.surface: An artistic person inside must be knocked out.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen in 'within-put' is a printing join; 'within' sets the word 'is' inside the arty type before its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To knock someone unconscious with drugs before surgery.
